guarantees.claim: incr is continuously assigned the value of incr_raw cast to type sp2v_e.
ctr_i_slice is assigned the bit-select ctr_i_rev[ctr_slice_idx].
sp_incr is assigned the 1-bit vector {incr}, effectively following incr.

assumptions.claim: incr_raw must hold a value that is a valid member of the sp2v_e enum; otherwise the cast may produce a non-sparse encoding undetected downstream.
assumptions.risk: A corrupted incr_raw propagates as a seemingly legal sparse value, bypassing sparse-signal fault detection and potentially corrupting the AES counter increment.

assumptions.claim: ctr_slice_idx must be a legal index within the range of ctr_i_rev; an out-of-bounds index yields undefined (X) on ctr_i_slice.
assumptions.risk: Corrupted ctr_i_slice can feed wrong counter value into AES, breaking confidentiality/integrity.

uncertain_points.claim: ctr_slice_idx is generated outside this chunk; an illegal FSM state or glitch could drive it out of bounds, corrupting ctr_i_slice.
uncertain_points.cond: during FSM state transitions or fault injection
uncertain_points.risk: AES counter corruption leading to plaintext/ciphertext exposure or tag mismatch.

uncertain_points.claim: The type-cast incr = sp2v_e'(incr_raw) performs no explicit sparse-validity check; a faulted incr_raw may propagate silently through incr to sp_incr, conflicting with the module's sparse-signal safety approach.
uncertain_points.cond: if incr_raw is corrupted or not a legal sp2v_e member
uncertain_points.risk: Faulty counter increment escapes detection, causing silent data corruption in AES-CTR output.
